column3: Dear younger me, I want you to hear this. Didi's inability to love you well was never a proof that you are unworthy of love. No, you were a child. You were not supposed to carry the responsibility of an adult inability to love you well. And younger me, I want you to listen to this and think about this very carefully. Maybe Daddy was available physically, but emotionally not available.

And maybe he was available physically and financially, but he never told you that I'm proud of you. Younger me. And that made you ask yourself, what is wrong with me? And maybe His criticism made you always ask yourself, is ever anything that I do ever good enough? And now you have grown up. You've become an adult that constantly need reassurance.

You always think that people leave and then you leave first. You always mistakenly mistaken boundaries as a rejection. Younger me, I want you to heal and heal for yourself. And your healing makes you to raise healthy kids because if you don't heal, it makes you raise broken children like the way you were raised.

The book of Psalms 10, verse 10, the book of Psalms chapter 37, verse 10, it says, though my father and my mother may reject me, But God will receive me. I want you to underline the word receive. Young me, God does not look at you as a broken and rejected child. He loves you. He receives you. He welcomes you. All you can do for yourself right now is to heal and move on so that you raise healthy children and you become a good version of yourself for you. Stay blessed!
